facts.fact: The National Population Commission's federal commissioner for Edo says the commission's birth registration system is fully digitised, with all registration data stored in a centralised national database and certificates carrying a QR code; he does not say where the entry is made, and gives no date, so the document's publication date is used.

The document says the National Population Commission and its partners have enabled more than 10 million children to obtain birth registration through electronic systems, a figure it gives no date for; its publication date is used. It describes births only.

systems.tiers: a centralised national database; state offices in Edo and Oyo named; certificates issued through hospitals after delivery

systems.system: Birth registration integrated with the NIN system
systems.owner: National Population Commission and National Identity Management Commission
systems.tiers: newly registered children obtain a NIN automatically, with occasional connectivity problems, per the Commission's Oyo State director; not connected to any education platform in Edo State

systems.system: NPC registration of pupils in schools
systems.tiers: officials visit schools and register pupils who missed birth registration
ward-based enrolment since February 2026, mobile registration teams and accredited agents, in Oyo State
